title: Tenali Raman Tale 132 (தமிழ்)
summary: A secret treaty document outlining military defenses on the northern border disappeared from King Krishnadevaraya’s private study inside ... [TA]
full_text:
A secret treaty document outlining military defenses on the northern border disappeared from King Krishnadevaraya’s private study inside the royal apartments.
Only three senior officials had access to the study: Minister Timmappa, General Veeranna, and Secretary Raghavan.
The King was in agony: 'One of my closest confidants is an enemy spy!'

Tenali Raman entered the private study.
He looked around the room:
In the corner, perched on a brass ring, was the Queen’s favorite grey African parrot, a gift from an Egyptian ambassador, known for repeating human phrases.
Tenali asked: 'Maharaj, was the parrot in this room when the document was stolen?'
'Yes,' replied the King, 'the bird has lived here for three months.'

Tenali sat quietly beside the parrot’s cage, feeding it pomegranate seeds and gently whistling.
For two hours, Tenali waited patiently.
Suddenly, as the palace bells chimed three o'clock, the parrot cocked its head, fluttered its wings, and began speaking in a low, conspiratorial human whisper:
*‘Quick, hide it under the saddlecloth... Meet at the Bellary crossroads at midnight...’*

Tenali listened intently: the parrot’s mimicry was extraordinary!
It did not merely repeat words; it imitated the exact nasal timbre, cadence, and breathy whisper of **Secretary Raghavan**!

Tenali immediately alerted the King.
A troop of royal cavalry was dispatched to the Bellary highway.
At the fourth milestone, they intercepted Secretary Raghavan riding a fast mare:
Hidden beneath the quilted leather saddlecloth was the secret military defense treaty, ready to be delivered to enemy envoys!

Raghavan was arrested and confessed his treason.
King Krishnadevaraya was awestruck:
'Tenali, while my spies searched the city, thou didst listen to a bird!'
Tenali smiled:
'Maharaj, conspirators speak in whispers believing walls cannot hear, but nature places sentinels where human eyes forget to look.'
The loyal parrot was granted a lifetime supply of royal pomegranates, and Tenali’s vigilance was celebrated across the empire.
moral: Truth cannot be suppressed by walls; innocent creatures echo the words spoken in shadows. [TA]
